item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
The figure shows how Mary spent her time one day.

[Image: Pie chart showing how Mary spent her time]

What percent of time altogether did she spend playing and doing homework?
item.figure_description:
A pie chart showing how Mary spent her time one day, divided into five labeled sectors:
- "Homework 10%": from the 12 o'clock vertical radius clockwise to roughly 1 o'clock.
- "Sleeping & Resting 40%": from roughly 1 o'clock clockwise to the 6 o'clock vertical radius.
- "Going to School 25%": from the 6 o'clock vertical radius clockwise to the 9 o'clock horizontal radius.
- "Eating 10%": from the 9 o'clock horizontal radius clockwise to roughly 10 o'clock.
- "Playing 15%": from roughly 10 o'clock clockwise to the 12 o'clock vertical radius.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Favorite Fruit Juice

[Image: Bar graph]

Lena asked her 20 classmates if they like orange, mango, or pineapple juice the best. She shows her data in the bar graph above.

She also drew a pie chart using the same data. Which of the following is the pie chart for this data?
reference_items.figure_description:
A bar graph titled "Favorite Fruit Juice".
- Vertical axis: labeled "Number of Classmates", marked from 0 to 12 in increments of 2 (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12) with horizontal gridlines.
- Horizontal axis: labeled "Fruit Juice", with three categories:
  - "Mango": bar height reaches 3 (halfway between 2 and 4).
  - "Orange": bar height reaches 10.
  - "Pineapple": bar height reaches 7 (halfway between 6 and 8).

Below are four pie charts, labeled A, B, C, and D, each divided into three sectors with distinct shadings and labels:
- White sector labeled "Pineapple"
- Cross-hatched/patterned sector labeled "Mango"
- Solid black sector labeled "Orange"

In each chart:
- A: The black sector (Orange) occupies less than half of the circle (around 1/4), the patterned sector (Mango) is small, and the white sector (Pineapple) is more than half the circle.
- B: The black sector (Orange) occupies less than half (around 1/3), the white sector (Pineapple) is about half, and the patterned sector (Mango) is small.
- C: The patterned sector (Mango) is large (around 1/3 or more), the black sector (Orange) is about 1/4, and the white sector (Pineapple) is about 1/3 to 1/2.
- D: The black sector (Orange) represents exactly half the circle (a semi-circle, 50%); the white sector (Pineapple) represents approximately 35%; and the patterned sector (Mango) represents approximately 15%.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.stem:
Class A and B each have 40 students.

[Image: Pie chart for Class A and bar graph for Class B]

There are more girls in Class A than in Class B. How many more?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two graphs representing student populations in Class A and Class B:
- On the left, a pie chart titled "Class A" showing a circle divided into two sectors. An unshaded sector representing one quarter of the circle (from 9 o'clock to 12 o'clock) is labeled "Boys". The remaining three-quarters of the circle is shaded grey and labeled "Girls".
- On the right, a bar graph titled "Class B" with a vertical axis labeled with values from 0 to 24 in increments of 4 (0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24) with horizontal grid lines. The horizontal axis has two categories: "Boys", with a light-grey bar of height 24, and "Girls", with a dark bar of height 16.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Mr. Johnson asked the students in his school about their favorite subject.

This pie chart shows how many students liked each of 5 subjects.

[Image: Pie chart titled Favorite Subject, divided into various sizes and labeled with Math about one-third, Science about one-fourth, History about one-fifth, Gym less than one-fifth, and Music less than one-eighth.]

Which graph shows the same information as the pie chart?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 30, Science value of 25, History value of 20, Gym value of 17, Music value of 8.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 30, Science value of 15, History value of 15, Gym value of 15, Music value of 14.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 20, Science value of 25, History value of 30, Gym value of 17, Music value of 8.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 25, Science value of 30, History value of 20, Gym value of 8, Music value of 12.]

reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart titled "Favorite Subject" is divided into five sectors: Math (the largest sector, about one-third of the circle), Science (the second largest, about one-fourth of the circle), History (about one-fifth of the circle), Gym (smaller than History), and Music (the smallest sector, less than one-eighth of the circle). In order of sector size from largest to smallest: Math, Science, History, Gym, Music.

Each of the four response options shows a vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled "Number of Students" ranging from 0 to 35 with grid lines every 5 units, and the horizontal axis showing five subjects: Math, Science, History, Gym, Music.
- Graph A: Math = 30, Science = 25, History = 20, Gym = 17, Music = 8.
- Graph B: Math = 30, Science = 15, History = 15, Gym = 15, Music = 14.
- Graph C: Math = 20, Science = 25, History = 30, Gym = 17, Music = 8.
- Graph D: Math = 25, Science = 30, History = 20, Gym = 8, Music = 16.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
This chart shows the types of cookies sold by the local bakery.

[Image: Pie chart titled Cookies Sold, shaded and divided into various sizes; sugar about one-fourth, chocolate chip more than one-fourth, oatmeal more than one-half, and vanilla about one-eighth.]

Which type of cookie did the bakery sell the most of?
reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart titled "Cookies Sold" is divided into four unequal sectors:
- "sugar": light-gray shading, occupying the top-right quadrant from the 12 o'clock position to the 3 o'clock position (a right angle, exactly one-quarter of the circle).
- "chocolate chip": medium-gray shading, occupying the sector from the 3 o'clock position to approximately the 5 o'clock position.
- "oatmeal": white (unshaded), occupying the largest sector from approximately the 5 o'clock position counter-clockwise around the bottom and left to approximately the 10:30 position.
- "vanilla": white (unshaded), occupying the sector from approximately the 10:30 position to the 12 o'clock position.
Visually, oatmeal is the largest sector, sugar is the second largest, chocolate chip is third, and vanilla is the smallest.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Pie chart with Birch (half), and the other half divided into Oak, Pine, Spruce]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four circular pie charts labeled A, B, C, and D:
- Chart A: Divided into four sectors. The entire left half is labeled 'Pine'. The upper-right quadrant is labeled 'Spruce'. The lower-right quadrant is divided equally into two sectors labeled 'Oak' (top) and 'Birch' (bottom).
- Chart B: Divided into four sectors. The left half is labeled 'Pine'. The right half is divided into three sectors labeled 'Spruce' (top), 'Oak' (middle), and 'Birch' (bottom).
- Chart C: Divided into four equal quadrants labeled 'Pine' (top-left), 'Spruce' (top-right), 'Birch' (bottom-left), and 'Oak' (bottom-right).
- Chart D: Divided into four sectors. The left half is labeled 'Birch'. The right half is divided into three sectors: a larger top sector labeled 'Oak', a narrow middle sector labeled 'Pine', and a bottom sector labeled 'Spruce'.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
